note: Independent re-audit against RFC 8050 Sections 2 and 3 after adding internal/plugins/mrt/rfc8050_message_addpath_as2_test.go::TestRFC8050BGP4MPAddPathAS2Subtypes. All four RFC 8050 Section 3 BGP4MP/BGP4MP_ET ADD-PATH subtypes (8 BGP4MP_MESSAGE_ADDPATH, 9 BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4_ADDPATH, 10 BGP4MP_MESSAGE_LOCAL_ADDPATH, 11 BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4_LOCAL_ADDPATH) and all four RFC 6396 base counterparts (1, 4, 6, 7) are now enforced end-to-end through OnBGPMessage, bgp4mpTypeSubtypeFor, localSubtype, and updateAddPath, and verified round-trip via mrt.ReadFile. TestRFC8050BGP4MPAddPathAS2Subtypes covers ASN4=false ADD-PATH IPv4 and IPv6 UPDATEs (subtypes 8 received, 10 sent) vs plain ASN4=false UPDATEs (subtypes 1 received, 6 sent) across both BGP4MP and BGP4MP_ET, asserting exact record count, MRT Type/Subtype, 2-byte PeerAS/LocalAS decoding, and byte-for-byte BGP message preservation, with discrimination records targeting dump.go::bgp4mpTypeSubtypeFor. TestRFC8050MessageCallbackPreservesEncodingAndFraming and TestMRTWinningCollisionPreservesOPEN continue to prove ASN4=true subtypes 9/11 vs 4/7 across both BGP4MP and BGP4MP_ET, all four NLRI locations (classic announcements/withdrawals, MP_REACH_NLRI, MP_UNREACH_NLRI), per-family/per-direction isolation (ADD-PATH negotiated for another family or opposite direction keeps base subtypes), live collision handoff OPEN fidelity, and complete message framing via observeReceivedWire and observedBGPWriter.observe -> selected_refresh_eor.go::complete. Verdict: enforced.
